rulings.challenge_claim: The verse-initial divine frame driving this boundary is byte-exact, but the row's corroborating inference that the divine title's recurrence distinguishes this oracle from the siege material before it is contradicted by the bytes, and the mandated rival is grounded on a speech frame that stands nowhere in the material it invokes.
rulings.grounds: Both strands verify from bytes, and neither touches the driver. The onset is sound: “כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת” stands verse-initially at MT 22:15 at BYTE tier on re-collation, and the divine-speech census lists that verse as its ONLY koh-amar site in ch 22 and classes it divine, not royal-messenger; the petuchah disclosed at MT 22:14 checks out against the marks inventory, correctly typed and correctly declared a non-driver. STRAND 1, upheld: the row's device_notes say the divine title recurs at the unit's own opening, 'distinguishing this royal-steward oracle from the general siege material that precedes it'. The title stack spliced from MT 22:15, “אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת”, sweeps at skeleton tier to 8 verses book-wide and FOUR in this chapter — MT 22:5 (prefixed, “לַֽאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת”), MT 22:12 (“אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת”), MT 22:14 (“אֲדֹנָ֥י”) and MT 22:15 — so three of the four stand inside the very material the title is said to distinguish this unit FROM. The inference is byte-contradicted. What actually separates the two is the frame's ROLE (verse-initial onset against postpositive signature), which the row never states; and the recurrence is skeleton-tier only, since MT 22:14 and MT 22:15 fail identity at byte AND at accent_stripped (the tsevaot token differs, and MT 22:14's carries a meteg, which the accent_stripped tier retains). STRAND 2, upheld and the more serious of the two: the mandated rival grounds the merge on a messenger formula 'shared' with the installation material, but the census carries exactly ONE koh-amar verse in this chapter, MT 22:15 itself — no such formula stands anywhere in 22:20-24, so the rival is grounded on a feature that does not exist. OL's replacement ground is byte-true and I confirm it: the second-person-masculine-singular address chain “כֻּתָּנְתֶּ֗ךָ”, “וְאַבְנֵֽטְךָ֙” and “וּמֶֽמְשֶׁלְתְּךָ֖” at MT 22:21 resumes the address of 22:16-19 across this row's own closing seam, and both witnesses read it as address — the staged WEB text at web:Isa.22.21 renders “and I will clothe him with your robe, and strengthen him with your belt. I will commit your government into his hand”. So the row's strongest real rival was never engaged. Severity low is calibrated right: the boundary rests on a verse-initial byte-true divine frame, the strongest tier-1 signal in the vocabulary, and neither defect reaches it.
rulings.remedy: Author work order, three edits, no boundary change. (1) device_notes: replace the distinguishing-title inference with the byte-true relation — the stacked title recurs at SKELETON tier across MT 22:5, 22:12, 22:14 and 22:15 (4 verses in this chapter, 8 book-wide), three of them in the preceding material, so the title does NOT distinguish the unit; what distinguishes it is the frame's role, a verse-initial onset against the postpositive signature closing MT 22:14; test = no device is claimed as distinguishing when the sweep places it inside the material it is said to distinguish from, and the recurrence carries its tier. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: re-ground the merge rival on the byte-true feature — the 2ms address chain at MT 22:21 resuming the address of 22:16-19 across the closing seam — and drop the shared-messenger-formula ground, which no verse in 22:20-24 carries; test = the test that killed the original, namely that every feature the rival invokes is attested by a sweep in the material invoked, with the count unit named. (3) device_notes: disclose that address chain as cross-seam cohesion arguing continuity, with the warrant that survives it; test = a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam is disclosed before the seam is claimed. observed_substrate_signals re-opens with the corrected corroboration. No respan proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's only declared substrate signal, a fresh addressee shift at its opening verse, is contradicted by the bytes: the addressee does not change there, and the second-person address of the officer sentenced at 22:15-19 continues inside this row's own span, undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Verified, and it strikes the row's single declared driver. The opening run “וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם” re-collates at BYTE tier at MT 22:20 and is a genuine day-formula scene onset (skeleton sweep: 45 verses book-wide, 4 in this chapter at MT 22:8, 22:12, 22:20 and 22:25), so a tier-1 seam is available there — but it is a SCENE onset, not an addressee shift. The newly named steward enters as the third-person OBJECT of the divine verb, “וְקָרָ֣אתִי לְעַבְדִּ֔י” (byte tier), while the grammatical ADDRESSEE one verse later is still the officer addressed from 22:16 on: “כֻּתָּנְתֶּ֗ךָ”, “וְאַבְנֵֽטְךָ֙” and “וּמֶֽמְשֶׁלְתְּךָ֖” at MT 22:21 are second-person-masculine-singular suffix forms, and with no morphology layer in the staged extract the form class is argued the sanctioned way — from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings, the staged WEB text reading “and I will clothe him with your robe, and strengthen him with your belt. I will commit your government into his hand” at web:Isa.22.21. The seam is therefore a referent-and-scene shift, not an addressee shift; the row's lone substrate key names the one thing the bytes do not support, and that address chain straddles the row's own OPENING seam undisclosed, arguing continuity against the cut. The internal contradiction OL names is real: the row's rejected alternative asserts at the FAR seam that 'the same addressee carries across both verses without a fresh vocative marker' — the exact opposite of what its opening claim requires, in one row. The rest of the byte work is clean and I confirm it: the marks inventory returns 0 parashah marks, 0 ketiv/qere notes and 0 special-letter segs inside 22:20-24, and the named-steward servant class is correctly kept apart from the book's unnamed servant-figure zones with no referent decided. ONE ITEM NEITHER REVIEWER CHARGED: the single in-span seg is cited as web:Isa.22.24 — an MT-keyed seg layer under a translation-side prefix, the very defect charged against the neighbouring rows in this same packet; ch 22 is identity-numbered so the digit lands, but the witness attribution does not, and it is credited here without the flag.
rulings.remedy: Author work order, four edits, no boundary change. (1) observed_substrate_signals: replace the addressee-shift key with the signal the bytes carry — a day-formula scene onset plus a referent change — since the addressee does not change at MT 22:19|22:20; test = every substrate key is attested by a run spliced from the row's own span, and the corrected key is re-derived rather than relabelled. (2) boundary_rationale: re-cut the opening sentence to claim a scene-and-referent onset rather than an addressee shift, arguing the seam from the day formula at MT 22:20; test = the test that killed the original, namely that the claimed shift is the shift the bytes show, checked against the 2ms chain at MT 22:21. (3) device_notes: disclose the 2ms address chain at MT 22:21 as cross-seam cohesion resuming the address of 22:16-19 across this row's opening seam, and state the warrant that survives it; test = the cross-seam sweep over the row's own seams finds nothing undisclosed. (4) device_notes: re-prefix the seg citation to the Masoretic witness (oshb:Isa.22.24), keeping the single-witness, count-only, no-position form; test = every seg-layer claim is cited under the witness that carries the layer. Correcting the driver re-opens strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence, and the rival's addressee-continuity sentence must be re-cut so it no longer contradicts the opening claim.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the row's case for standing apart from the installation material omits the strongest cross-seam cohesion evidence — a byte-identical catchword phrase binding its opening verse to the installation verse it separates from, plus the shared peg root. OL: the row's deliberate-recurrence disclosure is byte-false, because the postpositive divine signature it pairs with the day formula stands at exactly one verse in the whole header-bounded oracle, so the pairing it calls repeated has no second site.
rulings.grounds: Both items verify and they are DISTINCT defects at opposite ends of the same one-verse row. LF's, upheld and byte-exact: the place-phrase “בְּמָק֣וֹם נֶאֱמָ֑ן” at MT 22:23 and “בְּמָק֣וֹם נֶאֱמָ֑ן” at MT 22:25 are BYTE-IDENTICAL, cantillation included — re-collation of the 22:23 run against MT 22:25's bytes returns byte tier — and that phrase stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide, both of them here, straddling this row's own opening seam. The row's rival concedes only that 'the same figure is in view across both verses'; the verbatim device that argues continuity goes unnamed. TWO REFINEMENTS to LF's framing. First, LF cites the phrase and 'the shared root behind “וּתְקַעְתִּ֥יו” and “הַתְּקוּעָ֖ה”' but omits the stronger and simpler element: the peg NOUN itself recurs, “יָתֵ֖ד” at MT 22:23 against “הַיָּתֵ֔ד” at MT 22:25, sharing the skeleton “יתד” and standing in only 3 verses book-wide. Second, LF's root claim carries no tier and cannot be reached by a consonantal sweep at all: the mater in the passive participle breaks the contiguous skeleton, so a substring search for the root finds MT 22:23 and misses MT 22:25 — the mater-lectionis hazard class exactly. With no morphology layer in the staged extract, that root claim has to be argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings, or dropped in favour of the noun and the phrase, which are machine-checkable. OL's, upheld and byte-decisive: the row's device_notes call the signature-plus-day-formula bracket 'a deliberate recurrence' of 'the pairing used at the earlier scene-shift sub-unit'. The signature “נְאֻם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת” at MT 22:25 (byte tier) is the SOLE postpositive-signature site in the header-bounded valley-of-vision oracle — that census carries 23 verses book-wide and exactly ONE in this chapter — while the earlier scene-shift sub-unit opens on the day formula alone, “וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם” at MT 22:20 (byte tier), with no signature token anywhere in 22:20-24. The day formula does recur in the oracle (4 verses in this chapter), but the claimed PAIRING occurs once and has no second site, and the recurrence is asserted as deliberate with no tier label. Credits confirmed: the closing “הַמַּשָּׂ֣א” is correctly read as the common burden noun and kept apart from the verse-initial header class — the massa census lists MT 22:25 among its non-initial sites, so the row is right on the chapter's own trap; the setumah at MT 22:25 checks out and is correctly typed, though cited under a translation-side prefix rather than the MT key that inventory uses; and OL's last small point holds, the English gloss offered beside the closing splice covers a cutting-off verb that stands in the verse but not inside the spliced run.
rulings.remedy: Author work order, four edits, no boundary change. (1) device_notes: disclose the cross-seam catchword — the place-phrase byte-identical at MT 22:23 and MT 22:25 (2 verses book-wide) and the peg noun shared at skeleton tier (3 verses book-wide) — as continuity evidence straddling this row's opening seam, and state the warrant that survives it; test = a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam is disclosed before the seam is claimed, and the surviving warrant does not rest on the shared phrase. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: re-ground the merge rival on that catchword rather than on the generic same-figure observation; test = the rival names the byte-true device that supports it, with its tier and count unit. (3) device_notes: strike or correct the deliberate-recurrence claim — the signature stands at ONE verse in this oracle and the earlier sub-unit opens on the day formula alone, so the pairing has no second site; test = the test that killed the original, namely that a recurrence claim reproduces from a sweep naming its object, its count unit and its tier. (4) device_notes: re-prefix the setumah to the Masoretic witness (oshb:Isa.22.25), and re-cut the English gloss so it covers only what the spliced Hebrew run contains; test = quote/gloss parity holds on every splice and every seg-layer claim is cited under its own witness. Any merge of this verse into the installation material is a respan PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption.

rulings.challenge_claim: The inclusio driver is true at the tier the row honestly names, but the bracket is built without disclosing that the same imperative cry also stands mid-span; the row's declared speech-frame key asserts a divine-name adjacency the cited verse's bytes do not carry; and the word-bound proper-name digit reports the span's length rather than the swept object's count.
rulings.grounds: Three strands, all verified, none touching the boundary. The driver is honest and I confirm it: “הֵילִ֣ילוּ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֗ישׁ” at MT 23:1 and “הֵילִ֖ילוּ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֑ישׁ” at MT 23:14 are NOT byte-identical but ARE identical once cantillation is removed, and the three-token cry returns exactly 2 verses book-wide at that tier — the row names accent-stripped rather than overclaiming byte, which is the tier-disclosure standard met. STRAND 1, upheld: the imperative itself also stands mid-span at MT 23:6, “הֵילִ֖ילוּ יֹ֥שְׁבֵי אִֽי”, and the exact-token sweep returns 4 verses book-wide with THREE inside this row's own span (MT 23:1, 23:6, 23:14) — and MT 23:6's token is byte-identical to MT 23:14's, while MT 23:1's differs in accent. A cry recurring mid-span weakens its own end-of-span recurrence as a closing bracket, the row offers no occurrence digit for the object it brackets with, and the refrain-keyed substrate signal rides on the undisclosed reading. STRAND 2, upheld: the row's declared key asserts a vayomer-plus-divine-name frame at MT 23:12, but “וַיֹּ֕אמֶר” stands there with no divine name in its own bytes, and the amar/vayomer-plus-YHWH adjacency census returns ZERO verses in this chapter. The speaker is carried over from “יְהוָה֙ צִוָּ֣ה” at MT 23:11 (byte tier) — a defensible in-span inference, but not the census object the key names. STRAND 3, upheld: the word-bound check is byte-TRUE and the row is right on the homograph triple — the city name “צֹ֑ר” stands at MT 23:1, 23:5 and 23:8 inside the span, every one the two-consonant spelling, with no rock-epithet byform anywhere in this chapter and no adversary form — but the digit the row cites reports the span's length rather than the count of the swept object, which is the count-discipline rule inverted: name the object, then count it. Credits confirmed: both ketiv/qere notes in the span are disclosed at their bearing verses and both apparatus pairs re-collate at byte tier; both in-span seg sites are cited count-only and position-free; the setumah at the span's close checks out and is correctly typed. ONE ITEM NEITHER REVIEWER CHARGED: every one of those in-span disclosures — the two segs, the two apparatus notes and the closing setumah — is cited under a translation-side prefix for layers keyed to the Masoretic witness alone, while only the preceding-verse setumah uses the MT key; the disclosure layer is credited here as complete and correct without the witness flag applied to its neighbours in this same packet.
rulings.remedy: Author work order, four edits, no boundary change. (1) boundary_rationale or device_notes: disclose the mid-span occurrence of the imperative at MT 23:6 with the exact-token digit and unit (4 verses book-wide, 3 inside this span) and argue why the end-of-span recurrence still closes the unit despite it; test = the test that killed the original, namely that a bracket claim survives disclosure of every in-span occurrence of the bracketing element. (2) observed_substrate_signals: correct the speech-frame key so it does not assert a divine-name adjacency the cited verse lacks — name the carried-over speaker from MT 23:11 instead; test = every substrate key is attested by the cited verse's own bytes or by the census it names. (3) device_notes: re-cut the word-bound digit to count the swept object — the city name at 3 verses inside the span, no rock-epithet and no adversary form present — rather than the span's verse count; test = the count names its object first and its unit second, and reproduces from a sweep. (4) device_notes: re-prefix the two seg citations, the two apparatus notes and the closing setumah to the Masoretic witness; test = every seg-layer and apparatus claim is cited under the witness that carries the layer.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's undigited universal denial of any divine-speech frame inside its span is contested by the divine-utterance authentication formula standing at its third verse — the very formula cited at 22:25 in this same range as an oracle-closing signature — and that same verse is the row's one undisclosed seg site.
rulings.grounds: The defects are real but the headline framing overstates the first one, and one digit's object is unnamed. WHAT THE BYTES SHOW. “כִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה דִּבֶּ֖ר אֶת הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה” stands at MT 24:3 at byte tier, and “כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר” closes MT 22:25 at byte tier; across the two verses the relation is SKELETON tier only, since the verb forms differ. CORRECTION TO THE FRAMING: the row's denial is not simply false. It denies a massa header, a hoy onset and a divine-speech frame, and every enumerated census returns ZERO in this chapter — no verse-initial massa header, no hoy onset, no koh-amar site, no postpositive signature, and no amar/vayomer-plus-YHWH adjacency anywhere in ch 24. Against the frame classes the device spine enumerates, the denial holds. WHAT SURVIVES, and it is enough. (a) The denial is a universal carrying no digit-bearing sweep beside it, which is the one thing a universal in row prose must have. (b) MT 24:3 carries an undisclosed in-span divine-utterance authentication signal whose class the NEIGHBOURING row in this same cluster treats as evidence, closing that oracle on its twin — so the range applies two weights to one class with nothing reconciling them, and 24:3's possible closing function at 24:3|24:4 is never weighed. (c) The one in-span seg object, 2 segs at MT 24:3, count-only and single-witness, is undisclosed although the row engages the mark layer and the same object is disclosed at MT 22:24, 23:1, 23:13 and 23:17 elsewhere in this range — a real symmetry gap. DIGIT-OBJECT DEFECT IN THE CHALLENGE, new: the sweep is cited as '10 verses book-wide' immediately after the fuller formula is quoted, but 10 is the count for the broader divine-name-plus-utterance-verb adjacency; the quoted formula itself returns 4 verses at skeleton tier (MT 1:2, 22:25, 24:3, 25:8). The digit is right for an object the challenge does not name — the blend the count discipline bars. Credits confirmed: the remnant claim is exact and correctly class-split — the verb-family members stand at MT 24:6 (“אֱנ֖וֹשׁ”) and MT 24:12 (“נִשְׁאַ֥ר”) and at no other verse in the span, held apart from the noun, the collective noun and the personal name sharing the root — though it is carried by an unpointed mention while listed as a substrate signal, so it does not meet the pointed-splice bar that listing implies. The parashah statement is true: the inventory returns 0 petuchah and 0 setumah inside 24:1-13, and the petuchah closing the preceding unit at MT 23:18 is correctly keyed and typed. The boundary is safe on independent grounds: the other lens re-derived MT 24:3 as a candidate internal seam and found no addressee or scene shift accompanying it.
rulings.remedy: Author work order, four edits, no boundary change. (1) device_notes: give the universal denial its digit-bearing sweep and name each census object — 0 verse-initial massa headers, 0 hoy onsets, 0 koh-amar sites, 0 postpositive signatures and 0 amar-plus-YHWH adjacencies in this chapter; test = every universal in the row stands beside a digit-bearing sweep that names its object and unit. (2) device_notes: disclose the authentication formula at MT 24:3 as an in-span divine-utterance signal, with its tier named (byte at its own verse; skeleton against its twin) and the sweep object named, and state why it does not close the unit at 24:3|24:4; test = the test that killed the original, namely that the same formula class is not treated as oracle-closing evidence at one verse in this range and as nothing at another without a stated ground. (3) device_notes: disclose the seg object at MT 24:3 (2 segs, single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position); test = the span-relevant seg-disclosure symmetry sweep over 24:1-13 finds nothing undisclosed. (4) device_notes: raise the remnant mention to a pointed splice from source bytes with its tier named, since it is carried as a substrate signal; test = every substrate-keyed claim is carried by a pointed splice that re-collates at the tier it names.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row opens on a bare third-person-plural pronoun whose antecedent lies outside its span, leaving an anaphoric dependency straddling its own opening seam undisclosed; a supporting statement about the enumerated sung-praise sites is inaccurate as written; the divine-title key leaves a compound stack unnamed; and the setumah is cited under a translation-side prefix rather than the MT key.
rulings.grounds: Three strands verify; one is byte-false as charged. STRAND 1, upheld and the substantive one: MT 24:14 opens “הֵ֛מָּה”, an independent third-person-plural pronoun with no antecedent anywhere inside 24:14-15; the referent is supplied by the gleaning image closing the preceding verse, “כְּנֹ֣קֶף זַ֔יִת” at MT 24:13 (byte tier), which sits outside this row's span, and both witnesses read the pronoun as resumptive — the staged WEB text renders “These shall lift up their voice.” at web:Isa.24.14. The dependency is byte-true and argues continuity across this row's own opening seam, yet the rival sentence disputes only the far seam at 24:16 and the opening seam is left unargued. STRAND 2, upheld and confirmed against the controlled vocabulary itself: the row's prose states that the enumerated sung-praise sites 'begin at Isa.25.1'. They do not — the enumeration opens with a chapter-12 unit and only then reaches 25:1, so the parenthetical is false as written. It is also a register breach on its own: the sentence cites the governing strategy inside row prose, where the register purge bars strategy references outright, and the fix is to delete the apparatus rather than correct the verse number. STRAND 3, upheld: the divine-title key names the bare tetragrammaton, present twice in the span as a bare title, but MT 24:15 also carries the compound stack “שֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל” — a different count-object, unnamed. STRAND 4, REFUTED as charged: the setumah at MT 24:15 IS cited under the MT key in the row's own evidence refs, with the single-witness qualifier attached, so it is not 'cited under a translation-side prefix rather than the MT key'. The residual defect is smaller and different — the mark PROSE in device_notes carries a bare verse reference, which the convention reads as translation-side, while the evidence ref is correct; that is a prose-consistency slip, not a witness misattribution. Credits confirmed: the imperative form-class claim holds — “כַּבְּד֣וּ יְהוָ֑ה” at MT 24:15 is read as a plural imperative by both witnesses, argued the sanctioned way since the staged extract carries no morphology layer — and the operative-category deviation for applying the sung-praise label to a two-verse summons carries the one-sentence disclosure the category law requires.
rulings.remedy: Author work order, four edits, no boundary change. (1) device_notes: disclose the anaphoric dependency — the bare 3mp pronoun opening MT 24:14 taking its referent from the gleaning image closing MT 24:13, outside the span — as cross-seam cohesion, and state the warrant that survives it; test = a byte-true dependency straddling the row's own opening seam is disclosed before the seam is claimed. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: extend the rival to the opening seam, not only the far seam at 24:16; test = the rival addresses the seam the disclosed cohesion actually threatens. (3) boundary_rationale: delete the strategy-citing parenthetical outright — both because the claim is false, the enumeration opening at a chapter-12 unit rather than at 25:1, and because the register bars strategy references in row prose — and carry the category deviation on the bytes alone in the device_notes disclosure; test = no row field cites the governing strategy, and every surviving claim reproduces from the row's own bytes. (4) observed_substrate_signals and device_notes: name the compound title stack at MT 24:15 as its own count-object alongside the bare title, and make the mark prose carry the same MT key the evidence ref already uses; test = each divine-name digit names which object it counts, and mark references are keyed to the Masoretic witness in prose as well as in refs.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: the closing seam rests on a tier-3 single-witness mark alone — the tier-1 day-formula onset standing at the very next verse, the same onset treated as a driver at 22:20, 22:25 and 23:15 in this range, is neither quoted nor referenced, so the close is formally undriven. LF: the rejected-alternative disclosure names only the narrower 'own row for v.16' rival and omits a broader one, a recurring inhabitants-of-the-earth idiom tying 24:17-20 back to the chapter's own opening.
rulings.grounds: Both items land and they are DISTINCT — opposite ends of the row, and of opposite valence. OL's, upheld and decisive: the row's stated ground for stopping at 24:20 is a setumah at that verse, an object campaign policy bars from driving any boundary, while MT 24:21 opens “וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא” at byte tier — verse-initial, the sole day-formula site in this chapter, and the identical onset the neighbouring rows in this same range treat as a tier-1 driver at MT 22:20, 22:25 and 23:15. Neither the formula nor the verse carrying it appears anywhere in the row's prose or in its evidence refs, and the prose describes 24:17-20 as sustained imagery without saying why the sequence stops. The defect cuts in the row's favour: curing it REPLACES the barred tier-3 ground with the strongest tier-1 signal available, so the boundary is not in doubt — only its stated warrant. LF's, upheld in substance but REFINED in tier: the inhabitants idiom is real but it is not one recurrence at one tier. “יֹשְׁבֶֽיהָ” at MT 24:1 and “יֹשְׁבֶ֑יהָ” at MT 24:5 match at accent_stripped (skeleton “ישביה”); the plural construct “אֶ֔רֶץ” at MT 24:6 is a different form (skeleton “ארץ”); and the load-bearing link for LF's rival, “יוֹשֵׁ֥ב” at MT 24:17, is a plene singular (skeleton “יושב”) that fails skeleton identity with ALL of them — the plene-versus-defective and singular-versus-plural hazard class. The four are the only yoshev-family sites in the chapter. So the rival is a lemma-level observation, not a tier-grounded recurrence, and 'lexical tier' is not one of the four sanctioned tiers; the omission is real, the strength claimed for it is not. NEW FINDING, unengaged by the row and by BOTH lenses: a second-person-masculine-singular addressee marker stands at MT 24:17 — “עָלֶ֖יךָ יוֹשֵׁ֥ב הָאָֽרֶץ” — and both witnesses read it as address, the staged WEB text rendering “Fear, the pit, and the snare are on you who inhabit the earth.” at web:Isa.24.17, while MT 24:18-20 revert to third-person description. That address sits at the exact internal junction 24:16|24:17 where the row asserts the treachery clause 'threads without a fresh scene marker' into the terror imagery. An addressee marker is a tier-1 class under the evidence policy, and the row's continuity claim is never tested against it.
